channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
item.description: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

item.title: [DW] EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
item.description: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

item.title: [DW] Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
item.description: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

item.title: [DW] Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
item.description: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

item.title: [DW] European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

item.title: [DW] France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
item.description: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

item.title: [DW] Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
item.description: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

item.title: [DW] In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
item.description: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

item.title: [DW] Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
item.description: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.

item.title: [DW] Ethnic Germans in Kazakhstan face legacy of the Soviet Union
item.description: Kazakhstan is struggling to deal with the legacy of the Soviet dictatorship. Some 85 years ago, Stalin deported hundreds of thousands of people: Some 400,000 ethnic Germans living in the USSR were sent to Kazakhstan.

item.title: [EU Observer] Grandfather of Polish right Kaczyński stages court drama and calls for Polexit, as he launches his 2027 comeback bid
item.description: Kaczyński is hoping to make a political comeback in elections in 2027 in a coalition with two far-right parties, the Confederation of Liberty and Independence and the Confederation of the Polish Crown.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Allies fear Trump will target NATO in case of midterm loss
item.description: The U.S. president could move thousands more troops out of Europe or cut NATO funding as he seeks to cement his legacy, diplomats say.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU and Canada’s 6-month test of commitment
item.description: The Montreal summit launched work on a deeper partnership. Now 27 EU governments and Ottawa have to agree what that will mean.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Russian strikes leave thousands without power in Ukraine, says Zelenskyy
item.description: The Ukrainian president's remarks came as Moscow reported "significant damage" to an industrial facility in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Commission backs Tusk as he vows no compromise in court showdown
item.description: "Appointing the new judges lies within the power of the Sejm," Commissioner Michael McGrath told POLITICO.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Young Europeans know far more about Palestine than young Israelis, says MEP Lucia Yar after West Bank trip
item.description: Slovak MEP Lucia Yar reflects on her NGO-led trip to the Middle East: 'When I walk through the streets of Brussels, I see more Palestinian flags than I saw during my entire stay in the West Bank, where the Palestinian flag is perceived as a provocation'

item.title: [EU Observer] Sovereign AI, male-dominated by design: how EU procurement ignores women-led tech
item.description: Women face greater exposure to AI taking over their tasks, are less represented among the people who build the systems, and are under-financed as founders.

item.title: [DW] Serbia after Vucic: The winners are losing patience
item.description: After the Student List's election victory, Aleksandar Vucic's power apparatus is disintegrating. People want justice as soon as possible. But the losers still hold sway in the judiciary and administration.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Canadian scholar Henry Giroux on ‘gangster capitalism’ and why he supports Europe’s student revolts
item.description: Dr Henry Giroux has watched student revolts in Europe and is cheering them on. The scholar of critical pedagogy says ‘gangster capitalism’ is allowing the far-right to thrive and that culture is threatening democracy itself.

item.title: [DW] Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
item.description: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Hackers attack supermarket fridges in Belgium, Sweden and Luxembourg
item.description: Store fridges heated up to 50 degrees Celsius, mimicking similar incidents that plagued France last month.

item.title: [EU Observer] Zelensky stalls on his EU promises to protect gay rights, even as Ukraine rushes through minority-languages law
item.description: Zelensky’s government has shown it can move at lightning speed to please EU partners on some minority rights, yet same-sex partnership and hate-crime bills remain stuck in the Ukrainian parliament.

item.title: [DW] Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

item.title: [DW] What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
item.description: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?

item.title: [EU Observer] No extra funds for biodiversity at UN meeting, as vast majority of EU natural treasures left unprotected
item.description: Spending on repairing damaged ecosystems would need to rise fourfould, to almost $300bn to meet the natural protection goal countries set in 2022, a recent UN report found.

item.title: [EU Observer] Belgian parliament to vote on divisive new law allowing police raids on people’s homes, if they are suspected of harbouring an undocumented migrant
item.description: “The Belgian government may call them ‘home visits’, but that doesn’t change what they are: police forcibly entering private homes and traumatising families and children to arrest people", said one critic of the bill.

item.title: [EU Observer] Kursk and Krynky operations were disasters for Ukraine, new casualty figures show (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,709)
item.description: Ukraine also targeted a Russian refinery producing fuel for the army and aviation. A massive fire broke out.

item.title: [EU Observer] Culture groups ‘on their knees’ after 30% funding cut proposed in EU’s next budget
item.description: Culture, media and rights groups demand that European capitals oppose a 30 percent cut to €8.6bn proposed for AgoraEU in the EU's next long-term budget. “They picked culture because they think it’s an easy target, but it will affect journalists, artists and NGOs who are the backbone of our democratic society” said Nela Reihl, a German Green MEP.

item.title: [EU Observer] Neo-Nazi messages, links to Moscow, and Alice Weidel’s hypocrisy. 13 years of AfD emails have leaked
item.description: More than 400,000 emails exchanged by members of Germany's far-right AfD party between March 2013 and September 2026, effectively covering the party's entire history, have appeared online. What's in them?

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Let me die’: tortured migrants and rescue ships face off against EU-sponsored Libyan forces
item.description: Gaia Neiman reports from onboard the Humanity 1 rescue ship in the Mediterranean. The EU continues to fund the Libyan regime that is imprisoning men, women, and children, as a form of migration prevention. Survivors onboard an NGO rescue ship recount what they lived through, while Brussels sets its eye on a new migration facility in authoritarian-led eastern Libya.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Why is the EU introducing a new €2 charge on parcels?
item.description: From this Sunday, the EU is imposing a new €2 charge on parcels coming from outside the bloc. It comes on top of the €3 charge on small parcels announced in June.

item.title: [EU Observer] Why I’m protesting against the Palantir contract: a mother’s perspective on raising her son in Poland
item.description: Poland is not the first European country Palantir has approached, but other allied nations  have already drawn the line. In Switzerland, the Swiss armed forces rejected Palantir’s offers nine times. The military’s conclusion was that it was technically impossible to guarantee that  sensitive national data would not reach American intelligence services.

item.title: [DW] Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
item.description: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.
